Veils of the Inner and Outer Councils,  
  
I write to you from our camp in the outer ruins of the mursaat city of Bava Nisos. The alliance's progress into the city is stalled, blocked by some unusually potent magic. There are pockets of spectral agony and tides of Mistburn that come and go; it is a cursed place. Mabon knew this, so he kept the island warded.  
  
The nine of us have had the esteemed pleasure of serving alongside the late Fifth Veil, and though a few of you may yet harbor feelings of mistrust at his deception, I know some of you do not. Like me, he recruited some of you into the collective's Shroud. You rose in the ranks, tutored in spell craft and arcane protections that my most tempered exemplars would envy.  
  
Normally, I would pluck one of the more experienced Shroud members for a lesser job, but in this instance, I wonder if any one of you—someone else who carries Mabon's flame—might dust off your boots and step up to the mark?  
  
Awaiting your response,  
—Countess Anise, Eighth Veil

Saul,  
  
This'll need to be brief, as I believe my life to be at risk. The twins have been growing more and more impatient with my methods. Usually quite tractable, their voices have simmered to a calm eeriness that keeps me upright at all hours...positioned so that the window and door are always in sight. I don't even leave my room without a guard most mornings. I suspect that they're bored with the ritual now, working less fervently to hide their victims' screams from the other villagers than they did at the start. It's a bloodbath.  
  
And that brings me to the villagers... They've finally opened their eyes to the change in tone here. They won't enter any White Mantle structure unless ordered or dragged. They stopped eating our food. A few of them have even managed to escape. It was going so well until now, too; they were enamored with the result of our rebuilding efforts. I suppose too many have gone missing in such rapid succession. It's hard to blame every vanishing on a valravn.  
  
I've tried to slow our movements, but I worry that this has caused a rupture that I cannot fix. The twins are done with me.  
  
I beg of you, come back and control this.  
  
—Rhea

Just a couple more mouths to feed is how I see it. Unfortunately, the kids have already taken to 'em real good. Got grand ambitions of ridin' with them out to sea if the fog ever clears... I'm not gonna lie, when I first saw 'em I wondered how'd they taste seared on the grill with a little bit of salt. Marnie gave me a good slap on the back of my head for that. No way to treat guests.
